 Saqib Khan Takes Seven Wickets on Test Debut as Pakistan Pacer Announces Himself Against Sri Lanka
 Saqib Khan has announced himself on the Test stage in the most dramatic way possible, taking seven wickets on debut for Pakistan against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. The 31-year-old right-arm fast bowler…
 Published By : 
 Sports Desk , Rawalpindi 
 Last Updated: November 13, 2026, 09:45 IST 
 Saqib Khan holds the ball aloft during his debut Test in Rawalpindi, where he took seven wickets against Sri Lanka. 
 Saqib Khan has announced himself on the Test stage in the most dramatic way possible, taking seven wickets on debut for Pakistan against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. The 31-year-old right-arm fast bowler finished with figures of 7 for 130 from 34 overs on day three of the Test.
 Seven for 130 on day three
 Khan's spell shaped the match. Sri Lanka, who were 404 for 4 at one stage, were bowled out for 446, with Khan taking the wickets that broke their innings open. Pakistan had scored 434 in their first innings, and the debutant's efforts kept the visitors' lead to just 12 runs.
 Seven wickets in an innings on debut is a rare achievement anywhere in Test cricket. To do it at 31, in a first Test, against a side that had two centurions in its ranks, makes it rarer still.
 A debut in rare company
 Khan is only the fourth Pakistani bowler to take seven wickets in an innings on Test debut. He joins Mohammad Nazir, Mohammad Zahid and Abrar Ahmed on a very short list.
 His victims included Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva, both of whom had scored centuries in the innings, along with Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha. These were not tail-end wickets. They were the wickets of Sri Lanka's best batters, taken when the match was in the balance.
 A late bloomer from Karachi tape-ball cricket
 Khan's route to Test cricket has been a long one. He began in tape-ball cricket in Karachi, came through the academy system, and made his first-class debut only at the age of 29, in 2024, playing for Karachi.
 Since then, he has taken 81 wickets in 19 first-class matches, along with 15 wickets in 8 List A games and 12 wickets in 17 T20 matches. He was picked by Quetta Gladiators for the 2026 Pakistan Super League, although he played only two matches.
 He is yet to play an ODI or a T20 international for Pakistan. On the evidence of his Test debut, that may not stay true for long. A seven-wicket haul on debut is the kind of performance that changes a career, and for Saqib Khan, it has arrived after years of waiting.
